props.name: aria-label
props.description: The carousel's name, when it has no visible heading. The Root is a region landmark and needs this or `aria-labelledby`. Leave the word "carousel" out of the name, because the role description says it.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The id of the carousel's visible heading, the name APG prefers. The Root is a region landmark and needs this or `aria-label`. Leave the word "carousel" out of the name, because the role description says it.

props.name: children
props.description: The parts: a `Carousel.Viewport` that holds the `Carousel.Slide`s, and a `Carousel.Controls` row with `Carousel.Previous`, `Carousel.Indicators` or `Carousel.Status`, and `Carousel.Next`. Each feature is a part you mount, with no boolean prop for it. A server component can render the Root with server-rendered slides. The server renders no indicators and no page count, because the pages are measured after hydration.

props.name: defaultIndex
props.description: The page shown first when the Root owns the page. The pages are measured after hydration, and this page moves into place before the first client paint.

props.name: index
props.description: The current page, from 0, when the parent owns it. Pair it with `onIndexChange`.

props.name: onIndexChange
props.description: Receives every page change and its reason: `"scroll"`, `"previous"`, `"next"`, `"indicator"`, `"autoplay"` or `"action"`. A controlled Root that does not take the new `index` scrolls back to its own once the user's scroll ends.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The axis the viewport scrolls on. With `vertical`, Previous and Next point up and down. Give a vertical carousel's `Carousel.Viewport` a height.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: children
props.description: The `Carousel.Slide`s. The browser scrolls them with scroll snapping, so a swipe, a trackpad, a mouse wheel and, once the viewport has focus, the arrow keys work as on any scroller, and a flick stops at the next slide. The slides do not loop. A page change from a control scrolls smoothly, and jumps when the user prefers reduced motion.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the viewport. Give a vertical carousel's viewport a height, such as `h-40`.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The id of the slide's visible title. Without a name of its own, a slide is named by its place, such as "3 of 6".

props.name: children
props.description: The slide's content. A slide fully outside the viewport is `inert`, so Tab and a screen reader's reading order skip it, and in-page search does not find its text. A slide in view, peeking in or holding focus stays reachable.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the slide. A slide fills the viewport. Size it with a class such as `basis-1/2` to show more at once. Every slide stays a snap position, so the pages follow the layout: six slides three to a view make four pages. Space the slides with a margin on each one, such as `me-3 last:me-0`, and take it out of the slide's basis.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: children
props.description: The controls, in this order: `Carousel.Previous`, `Carousel.Indicators` or `Carousel.Status`, and `Carousel.Next`. With `Carousel.Autoplay`, put it first, and put the controls before the `Carousel.Viewport` in the source, so the rotation control comes before the rotating content in the tab order. `className="order-last"` on the controls still shows the row below the slides.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The accessible name. Unset, it comes from the locale dictionary.

props.name: children
props.description: The icon. Unset, it is a caret that points along the carousel's axis.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes, merged last through `cn`. A `px-*` class replaces the label padding only. The icon side keeps its own padding, which `has-data-[icon=inline-start]:pl-*` or `has-data-[icon=inline-end]:pr-*` replaces.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.

props.name: isPending
props.description: Marks an action in flight. The button blocks activation, dims, and stamps `data-pending` and `aria-busy`. It stays in the focus order, so a keyboard user is still on it when the result arrives. `focusableWhenDisabled={false}` takes it out of the focus order. `aria-busy` announces nothing, so say what is happening in the label, such as "Saving", or in a `role="status"` region outside the button. Put a label that changes with the state in its own element, such as `{label}`: page translation replaces a bare text child with its own nodes, so React's update to the old text node never shows.

props.name: isVisuallyDisabled
props.description: Makes the button look and announce disabled while it stays interactive. It stamps `aria-disabled`, and an explicit `aria-disabled` wins. Click, keyboard and focus still work, and a Tooltip on the button still opens. Use it for an action that explains on activation why it is unavailable.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

props.name: onClick
props.description: Runs before the control changes the page, and `event.preventBaseUIHandler()` there cancels the change. The pages do not loop, so Previous is disabled on the first page and Next on the last. Both stay focusable there, so focus that pressed Next onto the last page stays on Next.

props.name: onIntent
props.description: Fires once when the pointer's predicted path enters the inflated hit rect, for prefetching. Browsers without pointer prediction never fire it.

props.name: pendingIndicator
props.description: What a pending button shows in its leading icon position. When you omit it, a spinner shows there and the button's leading and bare icons hide, while a `data-icon="inline-end"` icon stays. A node replaces the spinner and does not animate on its own. `null` or `false` shows nothing and hides nothing, so the call site draws its own pending state. Fade that content with `group-data-pending/button:opacity-0`, not `invisible`, which drops the label from the accessible name, and give an overlay no `data-icon`.

props.name: predictionZoneSize
props.description: Pixels added to every side of the hit rect when predicting pointer intent.

props.name: delay
props.description: How long each page shows, in ms, before rotation moves on. Mounting the part turns rotation on, and it starts on mount unless the user prefers reduced motion. From the last page it goes back to the first. While the pages rotate, the slides' live region is silent. A new `delay` keeps whether the user stopped it. Keyboard focus on any element in the carousel stops rotation, this button included, as the APG pattern asks. So does a swipe, a drag that snaps back, a wheel turn or a press of another control. Keyboard focus in a slide's portal, such as a popover's field, also in a same-origin frame, or inside a custom element's open shadow root counts as focus in the carousel. Focus that a mouse press moved in does not stop it. Rotation pauses while a mouse or pen is over the carousel and while the document is hidden. Mounted with the Root or later, it starts from what is already so. It is paused under a mouse or pen already over the carousel, even since before the page hydrated on a device whose main pointer can hover. It is stopped with keyboard focus already inside it, as with an `autoFocus` field in a slide.
